step1_summary.chief_complaint: 4 days of upper respiratory symptoms now progressing to cough and fatigue
symptoms: Onset: ~4 days ago after close exposure to a sneezing colleague
Initial sore throat with painful swallowing for 1–2 days; now improving
Runny nose that is now mostly congestion/stuffy nose
Dry, persistent cough starting yesterday; constant throughout the day
Night sweats over the same 3–4 days
Initial fever that is improving with paracetamol/ibuprofen
Myalgias over the last couple of days
Mild exertional dyspnea; no dyspnea at rest
Appetite slightly decreased; drinking more than usual
No nausea/vomiting, normal bowels and urination, no rash, no ear pain or discharge, no photophobia, no visual changes

family_social_history: Family: Grandmother with type 2 diabetes; distant relative with eczema

step1_summary.vitals_exam_findings: No vitals or physical exam documented in transcript

V: Pulmonary embolism: Could cause exertional dyspnea and cough, but lacks risk factors, chest pain, tachycardia, and has clear infectious prodrome—very unlikely.
I: Viral upper respiratory infection (common cold, e.g., rhinovirus/coronavirus non-SARS-CoV-2): Sore throat, rhinorrhea → congestion, dry cough, low-grade fever, headache, myalgias, fatigue after known sick contact; typical 7–10 day course.
Influenza-like illness: Abrupt systemic symptoms (fever, myalgias, headache), cough, fatigue/night sweats; consistent with early flu course.
COVID-19: Cough, sore throat, congestion, headache, myalgias, night sweats; exertional dyspnea can occur; exposure setting plausible though not confirmed.
Acute bronchitis (post-viral): Dry persistent cough developing after URI symptoms; usually afebrile or improving fever, no focal chest pain.
Atypical or early community-acquired pneumonia (e.g., Mycoplasma): Dry cough and exertional dyspnea with systemic symptoms; short duration and mild severity make this less likely currently.
N: Lymphoma: Night sweats can be B symptoms; however, very acute onset with clear infectious prodrome and absence of lymphadenopathy or weight loss argues strongly against.
I2: Tobacco smoke irritation: Occasional cigar exposure could contribute to cough, but timing and systemic symptoms point to infection.
Medication effect: No ACE inhibitor or other culprit drugs reported; paracetamol/ibuprofen relieving fever supports infection rather than causing symptoms.
A: Allergic rhinitis: Congestion and rhinorrhea fit, but fever, sore throat with odynophagia, myalgias, and night sweats argue for infection rather than allergy.
E: Hyperthyroidism: Night sweats possible, but acute onset with URI constellation and fever makes this unlikely.
Diabetes mellitus: Increased drinking reported, but no polyuria/weight loss; 4-day acute infectious syndrome explains thirst better.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic progression from sore throat and rhinorrhea to congestion and dry cough over 4 days after a clear sick contact, with low-grade fever, headaches, myalgias, and fatigue; typical benign, self-limited course.

Systemic symptoms (fever, myalgias, headache, fatigue) with cough and night sweats could reflect early influenza; severity appears moderate and improving, but timing and symptom cluster are compatible.
Cough, sore throat, congestion, headache, myalgias, night sweats, and exertional dyspnea fit COVID-19; exposure plausible in workplace. No test data provided.
Dry cough emerging after URI symptoms with improving fever and no chest pain; could be evolving post-viral bronchial irritation if cough persists.
Dry cough, exertional dyspnea, night sweats could be early pneumonia; however, short duration, absence of focal chest symptoms, and overall mild course argue against at present.
